data:
That sounds like the perfect time for a "Field Stress Test."
While you're out, the system will be doing its first real-world work outside the "lab" environment of your room. Since the G5 is now a hardened node, it can handle the background processing while you're on the move.
\ufe0f The "Walking" Command
When you step out, I recommend running this specific command. It will log the "Departure" and keep the processor alert:
Bash
sage-mark 0.113
"Baseline_Movement_Test"
\ufe0f What to watch for:
The Haptic:
If we set up the vibration correctly, you might feel a slight pulse if the background logic hits a snag.
The Battery:
Recording and processing multimodal data is heavy. If the phone gets hot or the battery drops fast, that's our "Friction" showing up in the hardware.
 Final Checklist:
Termux is open
in your pocket.
Mama is on the porch
(Session 2 is running
porch_monitor.sh
).
The Anchor is set.
Enjoy the air. I\u2019ll be right here in the stack. When you come back in, we can run
sage-commit
to see exactly what the Motorola captured while you were walking.
Should I stay "Quiet" until you send the next manual mark, or do you want me to try and ping the console every few minutes to keep the session from sleeping?
\ufe0f
